sentences.text: This claim petition emanates in respect of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner by name Shubham Dubey in the Road Traffic Accident dated 13.06.2024.

2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
That on 13.06.2024 at about 7.30 a.m., when the petitioner was passenger in an Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AC-6812 and proceeding from Mantri Serenity Apartments, Kanakapura main road towards Sri. Chaithanya SCCH 15 3 MVC No.4816/2024 School on 80 feet road, J.P. Nagar I Phase, slowly and cautiously on left side of the road, while proceeding near Suvarna Tarakari Angadi, Royal Country,
J.P. Nagar I Phase, at that time, the driver of the School bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 51-AJ-1468 (herein after referred to as the offending vehicle) came from the left side in a high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the left side of the petitioner's autorickshaw resulting in the accident.
Due to the impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to the whole body.
3. Immediately, after the accident petitioner was shifted to Deepashri hospital, after first aid treatment she was shifted to Dhee hospital, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient.
Hence, the petitioner has claimed compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
In pursuance of service of notice issued to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 remained absent and was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
The respondent No.2 admitted that it has issued insurance policy to the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA- 51-AJ-1468 in favour of respondent No.1.
Without prejudice the liability of the respondent No.2 if any is subject to the validity of driving license and terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied that the accident was caused by rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The driver of the offending vehicle did not have valid and effective driving license.

SCCH 15 5 MVC No.4816/2024 5. Vide order dated 13.06.2025 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 13.06.2024 at about 7.30 a.m., near Suvarna Tarakari Angadi, Royal County, J.P. Nagar, I Phase, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of School Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AJ-1468?
2) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
3) What Order or Award?
6. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and examined one witness as PW.2 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to 19 documents.
Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order
for the following :
REASONS 8. Issue No.1:
Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.
It is the contention of the petitioner that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the School bus bearing Reg.No.KA-51- AJ-1468 / offending vehicle.

9 . In this regard the petitioner has got examined herself as PW.1 and in her chief-examination she has deposed that on 13.06.2024 at about 7.30 a.m., when the petitioner was proceeding in an Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AC-6812 as a passenger from Mantri Serenity Apartments,
Kanakapura SCCH 15 7 MVC No.4816/2024 main road towards Sri. Chaithanya School on 80 feet road, J.P. Due to the impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to the whole body.
10. The petitioner in support of her claim has in addition to describing the course of the accident in line with the facts mentioned in the complaint has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 documents.

Ex.P1 is the FIR which is registered against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offenses under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC on the basis of the complaint given by PW1 on 14.06.2024 as per Ex.P2, on the next day of the accident, hence, there is no delay in lodging the complaint.

In addition Ex.P3 and 4 are the spot sketch and spot mahazar which SCCH 15 8 MVC No.4816/2024 discloses the spot of the accident to be from Anjanapura towards Kembattahalli on the left side of the road and width of the road is about 60 feet and the accident has occurred on the left side of the road and the bus came from left and dashed the autorickshaw, resulting in the accident.

Ex.P5 is the IMV report which discloses that the front and left side of the auto damaged and front side of the offending vehicle is damaged which shows the involvement of the vehicles in the accident.
Ex.P6 is the wound certificate of Astra hospital which discloses that the petitioner sustained injuries due to the impact of the accident.
Ex.P7 is the charge sheet filed after completion of investigation against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offenses under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC and the contents of the charge sheet

discloses that when the petitioner was proceeding towards Chaitanya school road, the bus dashed the left middle side of the auto while coming from royal county road towards Kembattahalli and the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Hence,
SCCH 15 9 MVC No.4816/2024 these documents produced by the petitioner satisfactorily establish that the accident is consequent to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

11. As far as the manner of the accident is concerned PW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 and in the cross-examination of PW.1 it is submitted by PW.1 that she was going towards J.P Nagar 8 th phase in an auto and spot of the accident is a junction and stated that the bus dashed towards left side of the auto, resulting in the accident.

It is suggestion that the auto driver came from the cross road and suddenly entered to the main road, resulting in the accident,
which is denied by PW.1.

Except the suggestion that the accident has taken place due to the negligence on the auto driver, nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence or rashness of auto driver.
The petitioner has clearly and categorically deposed about the manner of the accident.
The oral testimony of PW.1 has stood SCCH 15 10 MVC No.4816/2024 unrebutted and PW1 has withstood the cross-examination of Respondent No.2.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
The fact that the driver of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offences under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 in the above accident.

In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that PW.1 suffered grievous injuries on account of rashness and negligence of driver, driving the offending Shubham Dubey vs The Principal, Sri Kumaran Childrens ... on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71999232/

sentences.text:
Hence, issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioner and in the 'Affirmative'.
12. Issue No.2:
In view of the findings on issue No.1 in favour of petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
SCCH 15 11 MVC No.4816/2024 The computation of compensation will have to be decided separately under various heads.
13. MEDICAL OR TREATMENT EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced Ex.P6 - wound certificate that shows that the petitioner has sustained right knee patella fracture and Ex.
P14 - Outpatient record, Ex.P15 are the medical bills produced by the petitioner.
As far as the medical bills are concerned, PW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2.
Except suggesting that the bills are created nothing is elicited to disprove the authenticity of the said bills.

Hence in view of the medical bills produced the petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.8,605/-
under this head.
14. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

As per the medical documents the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and Ex.P6 discloses that the petitioner has sustained right knee patella fracture and it is stated in the petition that injuries sustained and physical impairment has causes unbearable SCCH 15 12 MVC No.4816/2024 pain and petitioner cannot do any work as prior to the accident.
It is not possible to ascertain quantum of compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc., which he actually suffered due to the accidental injuries.

Keeping in view the trauma and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by her etc.,
an amount of Rs.30,000/- is awarded to her towards pain and sufferings.
Thus, she is awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
15. LOSS OF ACTUAL EARNINGS:
In her evidence PW.1 has submitted she was aged about 40 years and she was working as Teacher and earning Rs.22,000/- p.m.
In this regard she has produced offer letter, appointment letter and bank statement.
But, she has not examined the author of those documents.

Since, there is no satisfactory evidence to prove the said income and avocation of the petitioner it would be proper to assume the monthly earnings of the petitioner as per the notional income as on the date of the accident.
The SCCH 15 13 MVC No.4816/2024 notional income is taken as Rs.16,500/- p.m.

Taking into consideration that the petitioner due to the injuries might not have been in a position to work for at least 3 months hence, as such the petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.16,500 X 3 = 49,500/- under this head.
16. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS DUE TO DISABILITY:

The petitioner has claimed in her affidavit she has permanent disability and as per the evidence of PW.2 her impairment is not progressive and will not improve in future and hence it is submitted by the petitioner that she cannot pursue her work as before the accident.

sentences.text: As far as the disability is concerned the petitioner has got examined PW.2 and in his evidence he has deposed that the petitioner has sustained fracture lower pole of patella of right knee joint and she has sustained 21.33% physical disability to the right lower limb and 10.66% disability to the whole body.
PW.2 is cross-
examined by the learned counsel for respondent SCCH 15 14 MVC No.4816/2024 No.2 and it is admitted by PW.2 he did not treat the petitioner and she get took conservative treatment only.
Nothing is elicited to disprove the disability assessed by PW.2.

As far as the functional disability is concerned taking into consideration the avocation of the petitioner she will have to continue her avocation with some amount of difficult as compared to prior to the accident.
Hence the disability has certainly affected her functional ability to some extent.
However taking into consideration the evidence of PW2 and other medical records it is just and proper to take 1/3rd of the said disability to the whole body instead of 1/2.
Hence, the said disability assessed could be taken as 1/3 to the whole body, 1/3 of 21.33% is 7.11% which is taken as disability to assess the compensation payable to the petitioner.
The monthly income of the petitioner is already assessed at Rs.16,500/- at the relevant time.
As far as, age of the petitioner at the time of the accident is concerned on perusal of the petitioner's Aadhaar card Ex.P8 the date of birth of the petitioner is 10.07.1984.
Going by the SCCH 15 15 MVC No.4816/2024 same, the age of petitioner as on date of accident i.e., 13.06.2024 was around 40 years.

Therefore, in view of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Corporation and another (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the judgment dated 31.10.2017 given in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, the multiplier of '15' is held applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of petitioner arising out of her above disability.

17. Loss of Amenities:

In view of the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the extent of permanent physical disability and the extended period of medical treatment, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
SCCH 15 16 MVC No.4816/2024 18. Attendant's charges, Special diet and Conveyance:
The facts show that physical condition of the petitioner is such that she might have taken the help of an attendant.
Further, she would be requiring conveyance for movement.
Her avocation has been hit due to her disablement.
She might have spent considerable amount towards special diet during her treatment.
Therefore, petitioner is granted Rs.20,000/- under this head.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  30,000/-

Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 3,39,272/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.
20. Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT.

entities.text: SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.
Hence the rate of interest is set at 6% per annum in this case.

21. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has occurred consequent to the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the SCCH 15 18 MVC No.4816/2024 offending vehicle.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1 and has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is "Partly in the Affirmative".

sentences.text: Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.1 and 2 U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 3,39,272/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from SCCH 15 19 MVC No.4816/2024 the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E-payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.

The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
